chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Rehearsing with Don Redman's band and playing hearts
summary: Between jobs he rehearsed with Redman's band, where musicians played hearts and rehearsals started hours late.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: No, she didn't hit Ben. You know. But those are some times I tell you. But any way, during this time also in the interim -- you know, when I say I worked here and I worked there, but there were intervals where we didn't work, you know. And I would rehearse with Don Redman's

band, and Don was just a beautiful guy, very talented man, very talented man. He was a musical genius. Also he played to play dirty hearts. Most of the time we would go to rehearsal to play hearts. It was Syd Catlett again, Tyree Glenn, trumpet player who died, Red -- New Orleans.

Red Allen, yeah. And we would play dirty hearts, or sometimes rehearsal would start three hours late, we'd start playing hearts. But very memorable times. Most of the guys are dead now. Let's see, Tyree's dead, isn't he. Yeah. Red. Yeah. And yeah, we recorded during that time with -- I think it was during -- no, this was after. I'm getting confused because I worked with him before the war, this is when we did those things with Billie Holiday -- with Don Redman and the band. This is when they had Don Biase and Roy and Georgia Ali, I think I mentioned that, Kenny Clarke, and Jimmie Hamilton. Yeah, it was quite a date. [PAUSE]
